messages.subject: Error while installing rstan
parts:
Hi,

an error occurred while I was installing rstan on my windows 7 using R 2.15.2, after installing Rcpp, RcppEigen, and inline packages successfully. Hope you can resolve the error by looking at the message below:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
Installing package(s) into ‘C:/Users/Yoon Kyung/Documents/R/win-library/2.15’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
--- Please select a CRAN mirror for use in this session ---

** libs

ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rstan'
* removing 'C:/Users/Yoon Kyung/Documents/R/win-library/2.15/rstan'

The downloaded source packages are in
        ‘C:\Users\Yoon Kyung\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpI9DiZ7\downloaded_packages’
Warning messages:
1: running command 'C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-215~1.2/bin/x64/R CMD INSTALL -l "C:/Users/Yoon Kyung/Documents/R/win-library/2.15"   C:\Users\YOONKY~1\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpI9DiZ7/downloaded_packages/rstan_1.0.3.tar.gz' had status 1 
2: In install.packages("rstan", type = "source") :
  installation of package ‘rstan’ had non-zero exit status
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

So do you have any idea what is the problem here? Thank you!

Yoon

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error while installing rstan
parts:
One problem is that the g++ in the Rtools you installed is not available to R CMD SHLIB.  To make sure it is, you need add the the rtools to your system/user's PATH environment variable.  On this webpage http://mc-stan.org/windows-install.html, in which the steps of installing Rtools are presented. Make sure you have done 

Select Additional Tasks: check Edit Path and Save Version in Registry, click Next,

To double check that rtools is in your path, you can check path in a cmd windows as indicated in the attached snapshot. 

Last, you can also look webpage http://tonybreyal.wordpress.com/2011/12/07/installing-rcpp-on-windows-7-for-r-and-c-integration/, which is pointed out on the RStan getting started webpage.  But some steps on that webpage is not necessary.  But if you have installed Rcpp package in a path containing space, you might also have problem with the hello world problem.  You can simply install R in a path without space.  Or if you are sure you have got rtools in your path environment variable, you can trying install rstan without worrying about the hello world example. 

--
Jiqiang
